scenario_name: Common digital-dependency failure: shared project platform or cloud region
trigger: Multi-day availability failure, without data compromise, of a widely used construction-management or common-data-environment platform, its identity provider or its hosting cloud region
propagation_mechanism: Many contractors, owners and consultants lose simultaneous access to drawings, RFIs, permits-to-work, site diaries and payment applications; shared identity failure blocks fallback access
affected_sector_service: Project information management, site coordination, valuation and payment certification
plausible_effects: Programme slippage across many projects at once; delayed valuations and payments; disputes over delay entitlement; data-protection duties if data exfiltrated
early_warning_indicators: Provider status incidents; hyperscale regional impairments; credential-phishing waves against platform users; owner advisories
assumptions: Platform outage lasts several days; offline copies are incomplete; dependent firms lack tested manual processes
limitations: Not a forecast; no sector-wide platform outage observed in the period; impact depends on offline copies and contract float

scenario_name: Targeted operational disruption: major contractor or public-works operator
trigger: Ransomware or OT intrusion at a tier-1 contractor joint venture, its marine or plant operations, or a public-works operator's PLC/HMI estate during a time-sensitive programme phase
propagation_mechanism: IT shutdown and precautionary isolation stop access control, scheduling, vessel or plant control; subcontractors stand down; sequenced works miss windows
affected_sector_service: Site access, marine and tunnelling operations, water and public-works plant, building-management environments
plausible_effects: Schedule loss, standby costs, liquidated-damages exposure, safety stand-downs, owner and insurer claims, regulatory notifications
early_warning_indicators: Contractor incident notices; idle-vessel or site-closure reports; state or CERT alerts on internet-exposed OT; hacktivist claims
assumptions: Outage of one to four weeks during a controlling-path phase; workarounds cannot replace digital positioning or access systems
limitations: Not a forecast; Femern effects unconfirmed; Minnesota showed rapid local recovery in at least one town

trigger: Compromise spreading through a shared supplier's access, data or payment relationships: public-sector software supplier, managed service provider, materials manufacturer or payment counterparty
propagation_mechanism: Single supplier compromise propagates to many owners and contractors; data exfiltration triggers multi-controller notifications; materials or payment flows interrupted
affected_sector_service: Owner HR/HSE and planning systems, materials supply, invoice and payment processes
plausible_effects: Simultaneous delays and notifications across programmes; supervisory investigations of customers; payment diversion losses; supplier insolvency risk
early_warning_indicators: Supplier breach notices; regulator investigations of customers; leak-site claims against suppliers; BEC alerts
assumptions: Supplier serves a large share of owners or contractors in one market; customers lack exit or fallback
limitations: Not a forecast; supplier diversity and segregation (e.g. SANKO TECHNO isolation) can limit propagation
